SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE F& A REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 7150）
Section 2, Special Branch Station 35
REPORT
Date December 1st 1936

Subject Miss Barbara Miller (formerly Mrs. Little).

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Ross.

Miss Barbara Miller, a citizen of the U.S.A., was born
at Des Moines, Iowa, on October 10, 1902. She is a
journalist by profession and arrived in Shanghai from America
after making stop overs at Honolulu and Japan, some five
years ago. Following her arrival here she obtained employ-
ment first with the Shanghai Times and later with the Evening
Post and Mercury. In 1932 she joined the staff of the
North China Daily News.

On September 20, 1930, she was married at the local
British Consulate to an Englishman named J. C. Little, who
at that time was employed as a draughtsman with Reuch & Co.,
Sassoon House. Her married life was very unhappy because
of her husband's drunken habits. After a few years of
strifes, they mutually separated, the court giving her
permission to retain her maiden name. Little, in consequence
of his dissipated ways, was soon reduced to straitened
circumstances, and with the assistance of the Salvation Army
and the United Services Association was repatriated to
England during the early part of this year.

Barbara Miller, who makes no secret of her feelings
towards the U.S.S.R., took up, in order to obtain more
information about that country, the study of the Russian
language. In this direction she did not make much progress
and has by no means a great knowledge of that tongue.

In or about 1931 she made an unsuccessful application
for a passport visa to enable her to proceed to Moscow where
she hoped to obtain employment as a school teacher. The
application naturally was refused when it was disclosed that
she was going to Russia in quest of work.

日期：1936年12月1日

事由：芭芭拉·米勒小姐（前利特尔夫人）。

撰写及呈报人：探员罗斯 (D.I. Ross)。

芭芭拉·米勒小姐，美利坚合众国公民，1902年10月10日出生于爱荷华州得梅因市。她是一名职业记者，约五年前从美国抵达上海，途中曾在檀香山和日本停留。抵沪后，她先受雇于《字林西报》(Shanghai Times)，随后受雇于《晚邮报与信使报》(Evening Post and Mercury)。1932年，她加入《字林西报》(North China Daily News) 的职员队伍。

1930年9月20日，她在本地英国领事馆与一名名叫 J. C. 利特尔 (J. C. Little) 的英国人结婚，当时利特尔受雇于沙逊大厦 (Sassoon House) 的 Reuch & Co. 公司，担任绘图员。由于丈夫酗酒，她的婚姻生活非常不幸。经过几年的争吵，双方协议分居，法院准许她保留娘家姓氏。利特尔因其放荡的生活方式，很快陷入经济困境，今年年初在救世军和联合服务协会 (United Services Association) 的协助下被遣返回英国。

芭芭拉·米勒毫不掩饰她对苏联的感情，为了获取更多关于该国的信息，她开始学习俄语。在这方面她进展不大，对该语言的了解也非常有限。

大约在1931年，她曾申请护照签证以便前往莫斯科，希望在那里获得学校教师的工作，但未获成功。当得知她是去俄罗斯求职时，该申请自然被拒绝。

In April, 1934, she resigned from the North China
Daily News and proceeded to Los Angeles. Shortly after
arrival she was engaged by the Los Angeles Times - one of
the most conservative newspapers in America - as a space
writer. In this capacity she worked until the Autumn
of 1935 when she left San Francisco ostensibly bound for
Singapore on board the s.s. "Corneville," but on the vessel's
arrival in Shanghai on October 14, she decided to break her
journey and stay here. Through her own efforts she
succeeded in obtaining work as a proof reader with the Tass
News Agency, 20 Canton Road, where she is still employed.
She still entertains the idea of proceeding to the U.S.S.R.
and she hopes that by working for and assisting Tass, she
will be able to secure through them passport facilities
for the U.S.S.R.

While it is common knowledge that she entertains
radical leanings, she is definitely not a communist. She
is at present occupying room 622 in the Hamilton House.

D. B. Ross

1934年4月，她从《字林西报》(North China Daily News) 辞职并前往洛杉矶。抵达后不久，她被《洛杉矶时报》(Los Angeles Times)——美国最保守的报纸之一——聘为专栏撰稿人 (space writer)。她在此职位上工作至1935年秋，当时她离开旧金山，表面上是乘坐“科尔内维尔”号轮船 (s.s. "Corneville") 前往新加坡，但当该船于10月14日抵达上海时，她决定中断行程并留在此地。通过自己的努力，她成功在广东路20号的塔斯社 (Tass News Agency) 找到了一份校对员的工作，目前仍受雇于此。她仍然抱有前往苏联的想法，并希望通过在塔斯社工作并为其提供帮助，能够通过他们获得前往苏联的护照便利。

虽然众所周知她持有激进倾向，但她绝非共产党员。她目前居住在汉密尔顿公寓 (Hamilton House) 的622室。

D. B. 罗斯

Mr. E.L. Faupel, Mrs. B. Miller denied the attempt on
her part to commit suicide.

According to her statement she has been
suffering for sometime from insomnia and on the night
of January 8th before retiring to her bed she took
several tablets of Allonal hoping that the same would
help her to sleep. After a few hours, as she did not
feel any effect of the dose taken, she took another
quantity which had the necessary effect of sending
her to sleep. It appears from enquiries that she
has been in the habit of taking Allonal before
retiring to bed.

1936年1月14日。

续报：
美国公民芭芭拉·米勒夫人涉嫌企图自杀。

撰写人：副探长奥夫相尼科夫 (D.S.I. Ovsianikoff)。

继我于1936年1月10日关于芭芭拉·米勒夫人涉嫌企图自杀的报告之后，谨此说明，她已在广慈医院 (General Hospital) 从阿洛那 (Allonal) 中毒的影响中康复。1936年1月13日上午，她恢复意识，因此下午2点15分，驻华美国法警 E. L. 福佩尔先生 (Mr. E. L. Faupel) 和本人前往医院探望。当 E.L. 福佩尔先生询问时，B. 米勒夫人否认了她企图自杀的行为。

据她陈述，她患失眠症已有一段时间，1月8日晚就寝前，她服用了数片阿洛那，希望以此帮助入睡。几小时后，由于未感到所服药量产生任何效果，她又服用了一定剂量，这才起到了让她入睡的必要作用。经查询显示，她有在就寝前服用阿洛那的习惯。

Suspected attempted suicide by Mrs. Barbara
Miller, American citizen.

Made by D.S.I. Ovsianikoff.

At 8.59 a.m. on January 10th a telephone message
was received at the station from U.C.R. to the effect
that a foreign woman evidently suffering from poison-
ing was conveyed by the Fire Brigade ambulance from
the Hamilton House to the General Hospital. At 9.10a.m.
same date the undersigned and U.D.S. 36 Soong Yuen Leu
visited the Hamilton Apartment House, 6th floor, where
it was ascertained that Mrs. M. E. Roope, manageress
of the said apartment, called the ambulance at 8.56 a.m.
same date to take Mrs. Barbara Miller, American citizen,
to the General Hospital as she was found in the room
No. 622 occupied by her lying on bed unconscious. It
was believed by Mrs. M. E. Roope that Mrs. B. Miller
was suffering from poisoning. On receipt of the above
information the detectives visited the American Consulate-
General and reported the matter to Mr. E. L. Faupel,
U.S. Marshal for China.

At 9.25 a.m. Mr. E. L. Faupel accompanied the
detectives to the Hamilton House and in presence of Mrs.
M. E. Roope the room occupied by Mrs. B. Miller was
searched.

One small empty bottle formerly containing 12
tablets of Allonal "Roche" was found by Mrs. M.E. Roope
in an open suit case, of Mrs. Miller, where it was
lying on the top of clothing. One envelope containing
a check book of the American Express Coy. and addressed
to Mr. James Porritt was found by the undersigned in a
wardrobe. Several personal letters and passport
No. 14428 issued to Mrs. Barbara Miller in San Francisco
were also found in the room. The passport shows that
Mrs. B. Miller was born on Oct. 10 1908 in San Mateo.

1月10日上午8点59分，巡捕房接到来自 U.C.R. 的电话留言，称一名显然中毒的外国妇女由消防队救护车从汉密尔顿公寓送往广慈医院。同日上午9点10分，本人和第36号便衣探员宋元柳 (U.D.S. 36 Soong Yuen Leu) 前往汉密尔顿公寓六楼，经查实，该公寓经理 M. E. 鲁普夫人 (Mrs. M. E. Roope) 于同日上午8点56分呼叫救护车，将美国公民芭芭拉·米勒夫人送往广慈医院，因为她被发现躺在其居住的622室内的床上，不省人事。M. E. 鲁普夫人认为 B. 米勒夫人是中毒所致。收到上述信息后，侦探们前往美国总领事馆，并向驻华美国法警 E. L. 福佩尔先生报告了此事。

上午9点25分，E. L. 福佩尔先生陪同侦探前往汉密尔顿公寓，并在 M. E. 鲁普夫人在场的情况下，搜查了 B. 米勒夫人居住的房间。

M.E. 鲁普夫人在米勒夫人一个打开的手提箱里发现了一个小空瓶，该瓶原装有12片“罗氏”阿洛那 (Allonal "Roche")，瓶子放在衣物上面。本人在一个衣柜里发现了一个信封，里面装有一本美国运通公司 (American Express Coy.) 的支票簿，收件人为詹姆斯·波里特先生 (Mr. James Porritt)。房间内还发现了几封私人信件以及发给芭芭拉·米勒夫人的第14428号护照，该护照是在旧金山签发的。护照显示 B. 米勒夫人于1908年10月10日出生于圣马特奥 (San Mateo)。

From inquiries made among the servants of the house it
was ascertained that Mrs. B. Miller was seen by house
boy No. 11 named Ying Ah Meh(应阿才) at about 5 p.m.
on January 8th when she returned to her room from town.
At about 12 m.n. January 8th she was seen again coming
up to her room returning from town by houseboy No. 7
Loh Nun Jih(陸南傑). She came up to night porter named
Kiang Yoch Awen(江月民) in the Reception Room on the
6th floor and told him not to disturb her on the next
morning.
At 12.30 p.m. on January 9th the house boy No.11
Ying Ah Meh knocked at the door of room No. 622 as he
intended to enter and clean the same. After failing
to get any response to his knocking he opened the door
with his key and entered the room. He found Mrs. B.
Miller asleep and without disturbing her left the room.
At 3 p.m. same date he again entered the room with
intention of bring in a plumber to fix up a water tap
in the bath room. In view of the fact that Mrs. B.
Miller was still sleeping he again left the room without
disturbing her.
At about 6.50 p.m. a certain Mr. Russell telephoned
to Mrs. B. Miller but as she instructed the house boys
not to disturb her the telephone operator told the
gentleman in question that he had been instructed not
to disturb her.
At 7.30 p.m. the house boy No. 5 Woo Fong Fah(吴方法)
entered the room No. 622 to deliver the said message
to Mrs. B. Miller. He also found her asleep and after

1月9日下午12点30分，11号男仆应阿才敲622室的门，打算进去打扫。由于敲门没有得到任何回应，他用钥匙打开门进入房间。他发现 B. 米勒夫人正在睡觉，便没有打扰她而离开了房间。同日下午3点，他再次进入房间，打算带水管工来修理浴室的水龙头。鉴于 B. 米勒夫人仍在睡觉，他再次没有打扰她就离开了房间。
晚上6点50分左右，一位拉塞尔先生 (Mr. Russell) 打电话给 B. 米勒夫人，但由于她指示男仆不要打扰她，电话接线员告诉这位先生说，他已接到指令不得打扰她。
晚上7点30分，5号男仆吴方法 (Woo Fong Fah) 进入622室向 B. 米勒夫人传达上述口信。他也发现她在睡觉，之后

At 8.15 a.m. the house boy No. 11 Ying Ah Leh
reported to Mrs. M. E. Roope that the occupant of room
622 was asleep since the night of January 8 and that she
did not ring the bell to call any servant at all during
the day of January 9th. After receiving the above
report Mrs. M. E. Roope immediately sent No. 1 boy named
Sung Zeu Ching (宋祖清) to see if there was something
wrong with Mrs. B. Miller.
Sung Zeu Ching on entering the room tried to wake up
Mrs. B. Miller and after failing to get any reply from
her, he informed manageress of the house. Mr. M.E.
Roope after being told that Mrs. B. Miller was evidently
unconscious entered the room, called the ambulance
and sent Mrs. B. Miller to hospital.
From further inquiries made it appears that Mrs. B.
Miller arrived in Shanghai from America sometime prior
to October 31, 1935. On the last mentioned date she
rented a room in the Hamilton House and since that time
was residing there. She is employed at present by
the Shanghai Times as space writer.
From inquiries in the General Hospital it was
ascertained that on arrival there Mrs. B. Miller was
attended by Dr. G. Chambers. At about 10 a.m. same date
Mr. J. A. Porritt, merchant, room 26, 24 The Bund called
at the General Hospital and requested the sister in-charge
to remove Mrs. B. Miller to 1st class accomodations. He
signed the papers undertaking payment for the hospital
expenses. The doctor's chit states:-
"This is to certify that I have examined Mrs. Barbara
Miller and found that she is suffering from narcotic
poisoning. Her condition is serious."
G. Chambers.
Resident Medical Superintendent.
A copy of the above report is required by Mr. E.L. Faupel,
U.S. Marshal for China.

上午8点15分，11号男仆应阿莱 (Ying Ah Leh) 向 M. E. 鲁普夫人报告，622室的住客自1月8日晚以来一直沉睡，且在1月9日全天未按铃呼叫任何仆役。收到上述报告后，M. E. 鲁普夫人立即派遣1号男仆宋祖清 (Sung Zeu Ching) 去看看 B. 米勒夫人是否出了什么事。
宋祖清进入房间后试图唤醒 B. 米勒夫人，在得不到任何回应后，他通知了公寓经理。M.E. 鲁普夫人得知 B. 米勒夫人显然已失去知觉后，进入房间，呼叫救护车并将 B. 米勒夫人送往医院。
经进一步调查，B. 米勒夫人似乎于1935年10月31日之前的某个时间从美国抵达上海。在上述日期，她在汉密尔顿公寓租了一个房间，此后一直居住在那里。她目前受雇于《字林西报》(Shanghai Times)，担任专栏撰稿人。
经向广慈医院查询，查明 B. 米勒夫人抵达医院后由 G. 钱伯斯医生 (Dr. G. Chambers) 诊治。同日上午10点左右，商人 J. A. 波里特先生 (Mr. J. A. Porritt)，地址为外滩24号26室，来到广慈医院，请求负责护士将 B. 米勒夫人转至一等病房。他签署了承担医院费用的文件。医生的诊断书写明：
“兹证明我已检查芭芭拉·米勒夫人，发现她患有麻醉剂中毒。病情严重。”

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch Station,
REPORT
File No. 7150
2-36.
Date February 14, 1936.

Subject Suspected attempted suicide of Miss Barbara Miller.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Ross

Miss Barbara Miller, who forms the subject of file
D.7150, was admitted to the General Hospital on January 10,
1936 in an unconscious condition suffering from the effects of
an overdose of Allonal. Following her recovery on January 13,
she was visited and questioned by Mr. E. L. Faupel, U.S. Marshal
for China. Apart from admitting that she had been in the
habit of taking Allonal as a sedative for insomnia, she strongly
denied that she had attempted to commit suicide.
She was discharged from hospital on January 18 and returned
to her flat No. 622, Hamilton House.
Prior to entering the hospital she was on the staff of
the Shanghai Times. It appears that Miss Miller had severed
connections with the Tass News Agency sometime ago in consequence
of the long hours she was compelled to work for which she was
poorly paid in return.
As her health had suffered considerably owing to the
continued use of drugs, she was prevailed upon by certain of
her intimate friends to take a holiday in order to recuperate,
and in this connection she sailed for the United States
(Los Angeles) in the "General Sherman" on February 4, 1936.

A copy of Central S.R. Mis. Report
No 23/36, bearing on this matter
is attached herewith. JAR
D. I. Ross
Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch) DC (Crime)
Information
Jno Robertson

日期：1936年2月14日。

事由：芭芭拉·米勒小姐涉嫌企图自杀。

撰写及呈报人：探员 D. I. 罗斯

档案 D.7150 所涉之芭芭拉·米勒小姐，于1936年1月10日因服用过量阿洛那导致昏迷而被送入广慈医院。1月13日康复后，驻华美国法警 E. L. 福佩尔先生对她进行了探访和问询。除了承认她有服用阿洛那作为失眠镇静剂的习惯外，她强烈否认曾企图自杀。
她于1月18日出院，回到汉密尔顿公寓622室寓所。
入院前，她是《字林西报》(Shanghai Times) 的职员。看来米勒小姐此前已因工作时间长且报酬低而与塔斯社断绝了联系。
由于长期用药，她的健康受到极大损害，几位亲密朋友劝她休假以恢复健康，为此，她于1936年2月4日乘坐“谢尔曼将军”号 (General Sherman) 轮船前往美国（洛杉矶）。

随函附上与此事相关的中央巡捕房杂项报告第23/36号副本。JAR

speaking of diplomas, got hers at
Stanford a while back and has
since busied herself in collecting Far

芭芭拉·米勒·巴克
在加利福尼亚，计划撰写
关于中国的女性视角书籍

当来自上海和洛杉矶的芭芭拉·米勒小姐最近从远东返回美国时，她获得了大量的公众关注，包括在旧金山的《纪事报》和《考察家报》上刊登的照片，配图说明称她计划从“女性角度”撰写一本关于东方的书。
《考察家报》的航运专栏也刊登了以下关于米勒小姐的简讯：
“安息日迎来了从东方驶来的‘谢尔曼将军号’轮船，随船抵达的是芭芭拉·米勒小姐，这位洛杉矶姑娘不久前在斯坦福大学获得了学位，此后一直忙于收集远东资料，以撰写一本将从米勒小姐所称的女性角度探讨东方的书籍。
‘你在那边把男人们都搞定了，米勒小姐。’”
